study type: Prospective longitudinal survey, as part of a cluster randomized trial (OptiBIRTH)
exposure: Match ERCS-ERCS (preference for caesarean section, actual mode of birth elective repeat caesarean section)
Match VBAC-VBAC (preference for vaginal birth, actual mode of birth vaginal birth)
Antenatal birth mode preferences (vaginal birth after caesarean [VBAC] or elective repeat caesarean section [ERCS])
Match ERCS-EMCS (preference for caesarean section, actual mode of birth emergency repeat caesarean section)
Mismatch VBAC-EMCS (preference for vaginal birth, actual mode of birth emergency repeat caesarean section)
Mismatch VBAC-ERCS (preference for vaginal birth, actual mode of birth elective repeat caesarean section)
outcome: Postnatal Health Related Quality of Life (HRQoL)
cohort: 862 women with one previous caesarean section from Germany, Ireland, and Italy
finding: Women who preferred VBAC but underwent ERCS had significantly lower postnatal HRQoL compared to those who preferred and achieved VBAC.
mod_finding: Women with a preference for vaginal birth who gave birth by elective repeat caesarean section had significantly lower HRQoL at three months postnatal.
